summary: CCC-built 1938 fire lookout on Tall Peak in the Ouachita National Forest; NRHP-listed 1993, inactive and vandalized, cab door locked at 2021 visits.

facts.design: 12x12 live-in wooden cab with catwalk on a one-story stone base (NHLR); the 1993 NRHP form describes a two-story fieldstone and wood structure with an observation deck
facts.status_note: Standing but deteriorated: NRHP form notes vandalism and repairs; 2021 visit reports say it needs paint and the building door was locked

staffing.status: not staffed; inactive as a lookout for many years

access.note: On Ouachita National Forest land; the 2021 NHLR visit report says it is reached only by a hike of more than four miles. The building door was locked. No closure notice was found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Walk-in from Shady Lake recreation area per a 2020 trip report. Wikipedia says a forest service road reaches it; the 2021 NHLR visit report says only by a 4+ mile hike. Check with the Mena Ranger District before giving route advice.

events.note: Built circa 1938 by the 742nd Company of the Arkansas CCC from the Mena camp as a fire and observation tower
Added to the National Register of Historic Places (ref. 93001077) on October 20, 1993

Registered July 16, 1996 as US 183, AR 2; nominated by Michael A. Pfeiffer, FFLA
NHLR visit reports of July 10 and September 25, 2021: needs paint, building door locked, catwalk okay, reached only by a 4+ mile hike, not staffed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR describes a one-story stone base under a 12x12 live-in cab; the 1993 NRHP form describes a two-story fieldstone and wood structure. The story reports both descriptions.

Wikipedia says a forest service road off Polk County 64 reaches the tower, and the NRHP registration form places it on Forest Service Road #38A. The 2021 NHLR visit reports say it is only accessible by a 4+ mile hike. No source says whether the road is closed or gated, so the story reports the disagreement without choosing.

notes_for_editor: Built year 1938 in the brief is confirmed by four sources (NRHP circa 1938, NHLR 1938, Wikipedia about 1938, trip report 1938). The NRHP registration form (received by the state 14 Sept 1993) says the tower was deteriorated at that time; its condition since then comes only from two 2021 NHLR visit reports and a 2020 trip report. No source found the date the tower stopped being staffed, so staffing is dated as of 2021. Access wording needs checking with the Mena Ranger District before publication, since the road-versus-hike conflict is unresolved. The brief's elevation (698.6 m) matches the NHLR's 2,292 ft (699 m). Not read: Living New Deal page (403), ARGenWeb Mena and Oden lookouts page, Grokipedia. Photos not added: the NHLR shows a 1996 photo and a September 2021 photo courtesy Travis Howk, and the trip report shows a 1963 photo courtesy Central US Lookouts, but no image URLs or licences were checked.
